primary_hypothesis: A repurposed medicine for BUB1B-related mosaic variegated aneuploidy earns its next experiment only if it acts in the compensating direction on the bottleneck the decisive experiment is built to measure — residual BubR1 abundance and checkpoint function, both of which are UNKNOWN in this child — passes this patient's constraint gates with every safety axis those gates cannot see declared rather than counted as clear, and rests on an approved product with a dated label. Under that rule the single named candidate is niacin (nicotinic acid), an approved NAD+ precursor acting through the SIRT2–BubR1 stabilization axis, carried as a conditional research hypothesis and not a recommendation: its oncology axis is contradictory and its growth axis unassessed. It is overturned if NAD+ repletion in patient-derived cells fails to raise BubR1 protein, fails to correct the checkpoint defect, or raises the aneuploid fraction of the surviving population — a fraction, never raw survival, because a real checkpoint rescue can raise overall survival.
